Convert counts to rates per population or weighted-population denominator

Source: R/org.R
op_rate.Rd

Joins prescribing data to denominators by month (and organisation) and computes numerator / denominator * per.

Usage

op_rate(
  x,
  details,
  numerator = "items",
  denominator = "total_list_size",
  per = 1000,
  name = "rate"
)

Arguments

x

Data frame from op_spending() or op_spending_ab().

details

Data frame from op_org_details() at the same organisation level.

numerator

Column of x to use (default "items").

denominator

Column of details (default "total_list_size"; for antibacterial prescribing "star_pu_oral_antibacterial_items" is the usual age-sex weighted choice).

per

Scaling factor (default 1000).

name

Name of the new column. Default "rate".

Value

x with the denominator and the new rate column added; the rate definition is stored in the "rate_label" attribute and used by the plotting functions for axis labels. Rows without a matching denominator get NA.

Examples

x <- data.frame(date = as.Date(c("2025-01-01", "2025-02-01")), org_id = "A",
                items = c(120, 150))
d <- data.frame(date = as.Date(c("2025-01-01", "2025-02-01")), org_id = "A",
                total_list_size = c(60000, 60100))
op_rate(x, d)
#>         date org_id items total_list_size    rate
#> 1 2025-01-01      A   120           60000 2.00000
#> 2 2025-02-01      A   150           60100 2.49584
